defects_found_before_review: A failure *detail* string leaked a credential while the structured body was redacted. Redaction was centralised into safe_failure() so an adapter cannot redact one and forget the other; both the fixture and Zen adapters use it.
The SSE byte decoder only emitted decoded text when a partial character remained, which is almost never, so most streams parsed as empty. Found by the streaming tests before any gate check.
The SSE parser kept consuming records after the [DONE] sentinel when the sentinel and later records arrived in one read.
The fixture transport's unsupported-setting report read the request after it had been deleted from scope.

environment.network: none used; the adapter layer imports no http/requests/socket/urllib, asserted by AST inspection

gate_criteria.criterion: adapter output matches the result contract
gate_criteria.evidence: Every adapter outcome is re-validated against GenerationResult from its own serialized form in tests/contract/test_g03_gate.py, parametrized over the fixture and Zen adapters. A failure yields no result rather than an accepted empty one; an adapter result can contribute at most one accepted sample.

gate_criteria.criterion: chunks are not counted as tokens
gate_criteria.evidence: test_no_adapter_derives_tokens_from_chunks streams 200 chunks and asserts the only token count is the 2 the endpoint reported. StreamAssembly.token_rate() returns None unless a reported output-token count and a measured duration are both present; there is no chunk-to-token helper anywhere in the module. Substituting chunk_count for a missing token count is mutation-detected.

safe_failure() redacts both the detail string and the structured body. Tests assert a canary is absent from the detail, from failure.to_dict() and from the whole outcome for both adapters, and that a known credential header name is redacted while ordinary headers stay readable.

An unsupported setting is reported with the value that was requested and a reason, never dropped. The base stream() refuses outright rather than returning a non-streamed result labelled as streamed, so no timing measurement can be fabricated. Mutating the catalog to invent streaming support is mutation-detected.

gate_criteria.criterion: production adapter behavior is demonstrated against fixture protocol transcripts
gate_criteria.evidence: ZenAdapter is driven by a recorded transcript loaded from disk (ZenAdapter.from_path) and runs its real normalisation: catalog snapshotting, usage extraction under three key conventions, finish-reason mapping, tool-call extraction and error mapping. The same code path serves a live capture, so the offline suite exercises production behaviour rather than a double.

source_revision.recompute_command: find . -type f \( -name '*.py' -o -name '*.toml' -o -name '*.md' -o -name '*.json' -o -name '*.yml' -o -name 'py.typed' -o -name 'constraints-dev.txt' \) -not -path './.venv/*' -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' -not -path './implementation/evidence/*' -not -path './implementation/tasks.json' | sort | while read -r f; do printf '%s  %s\n' "$(sha256sum "$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)" "${f#./}"; done | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1

T03A.evidence: tests/contract/test_provider_contract.py (47 tests) covers a normal response, all eight failure kinds with their retryable classification, absent usage, partially reported usage, reported zero usage, unsupported settings, streaming refusal, catalog normalisation and bundle validation.

T03B.evidence: tests/contract/test_zen_adapter.py (63 tests) covers normal/empty/malformed catalogs, authentication and permission and 404 and 429 and 5xx and timeout failures, usage absence in three key conventions, tool responses, finish-reason mapping including an unrecognised reason, and an explicit test that no stealth alias is hardcoded in the adapter source.

T03C.evidence: tests/contract/test_streaming.py (43 tests) covers records split across reads, several records in one read, byte-at-a-time delivery, multi-byte characters split across a read boundary including an emoji and a surrogate-escaped payload, reasoning-only chunks, usage-only terminal chunks, finish chunks, stream interruption, an unparsable record mid-stream, and chunk-count isolation from token counts.
